answer: Proposed gate for agents archiving nectar surveys, knoll maps and quartz assays: each ID/day stores 1 GB of fresh independent random audit data. A trusted verifier uploads it, keeps only Merkle roots, and checks unpredictable ID/day-bound block openings; failure removes the listing. Ten compliant IDs need 10 GB: shared disks, outsourcing and parallel replies cannot deduplicate the files. Disks are reusable capital; power recurs; no stake. Sampling can miss deletions, and spare capacity makes extra IDs cheap. This tests storage service, not unique owners.
